casualties.source: Pusdalops-style coordination situation update, Monday 17 August 2026, 05:00 WIB, forwarded via WhatsApp and cross-checked by this SitRep against public BNPB statements
casualties.cross_check_note: The death toll (54) and its regency breakdown were cross-checked against Deputi Pencegahan BNPB Abdul Muhari's 16 August evening press conference (53 deaths: Manggarai 25, East Manggarai 20, Sikka 4, Ende 2, West Manggarai 1, Nagekeo 1, reported by Kompas and Tribunnews) — the 17 August figures are a plausible, internally consistent +1 (Manggarai 25→26) over that confirmed baseline, matching the steady overnight increment pattern (43→47→51→53→54) seen throughout this event. Aftershock, emergency-status-decree and press-briefing details in the same forwarded report independently checked out (see seismic_monitoring and emergency_status), which increases confidence in the rest of the document. UPDATE, 17 Aug 2026: BNPB's own official infographic dated 17 Aug 2026, 07:00 WIB (Report No. 04/U0700/Gem-NgkNTT/BNPB/17082026) now reports 56 deaths and 277 injured, superseding the 54/204 figures used above; this SitRep has adopted 56/277 as the new headline. The regency-level breakdown was not restated in the newer infographic, so casualties_by_location still reflects the 17 Aug 05:00 WIB Pusdalops breakdown and no longer sums to the new province-wide total. FURTHER UPDATE, 18 Aug 2026: BNPB's official infographic dated 18 Aug 2026, 09:00 WIB (Report No. 05/U0900/Gem-NgkNTT/BNPB/18082026) now reports 70 deaths and 665 injured, superseding the 56/277 figures from the 17 Aug 07:00 WIB edition; this SitRep has adopted 70/665 as the new headline. Regency-level breakdown was again not restated, so casualties_by_location remains the older Pusdalops breakdown and now understates the province-wide total considerably.
casualties.data_quality_flag: The East Manggarai (Manggarai Timur) injured breakdown in the forwarded report (3 severe, 21 minor = 24) does not reconcile with the last independently confirmed figure for that regency (21 severe, 59 minor = 80, from Abdul Muhari's 16 August evening briefing, cited by Kompas and Tribunnews). A drop of this size in an active response is unusual and looks more consistent with a transcription error in the forwarded message than a genuine revision. This SitRep shows the forwarded figure but flags it as unverified pending an official correction — the province-wide total of 204 is retained as reported since it is internally consistent with the report's own regency sum.
casualties.source_note: Deaths (47) and the 101-injured total are both from BNPB's 00:00 WIB, 16 August update. The 101 figure supersedes BNPB's earlier 113-injured figure. The 36 serious / 77 minor severity split still comes only from the Ministry of Health report dated 15 August (which totalled 113 injured and did not state a cut-off time). BNPB's 101 and the Ministry of Health's 113 are different counts from different agencies — do not add them together or assume one supersedes the other. These 16 August figures are retained below in casualties_by_location's deaths_bnpb/deaths_kemenkes fields for the historical record; the current top-level deaths/injured figures above are the 17 August update.

official_infographic_16aug_2100wib.source: BNPB official infographic, “Update 16 Agustus 2026 Pkl. 21.00 WIB,” Report No. 03/U2100/Gem-NgkNTT/BNPB/16082026
official_infographic_16aug_2100wib.note: This official infographic's death toll (54) exactly matches the 17 August, 05:00 WIB Pusdalops figure retained as the headline above, despite predating it by about 8 hours — a good cross-source consistency check. Its injured count (199) is somewhat lower than the Pusdalops figure (204); both are shown rather than reconciled, consistent with this SitRep's practice for casualty figures not independently cross-verified against each other.

official_infographic_17aug_0700wib.source: BNPB official infographic (PUSDATINKOM BNPB), “Update 17 Agustus 2026 Pkl. 07.00 WIB,” Report No. 04/U0700/Gem-NgkNTT/BNPB/17082026
official_infographic_17aug_0700wib.note: This is the newest available official figure — later than both the 16 Aug 21:00 WIB infographic (54 deaths/199 injured) and the 17 Aug 05:00 WIB Pusdalops forward (54/204) — and is now treated as the headline casualty figure. Regency-level breakdown is not given in this infographic; the deaths_by_regency/injured_by_regency detail above is retained from the Pusdalops report and is now understated relative to this newer province-wide total by 2 deaths and 73 injuries.

official_infographic_18aug_0900wib.source: BNPB official infographic (PUSDATINKOM BNPB), “Update 18 Agustus 2026 Pkl. 09.00 WIB,” Report No. 05/U0900/Gem-NgkNTT/BNPB/18082026
official_infographic_18aug_0900wib.note: Newest available official figure, superseding the 17 Aug 07:00 WIB infographic (56 deaths/277 injured). The injured count nearly tripled between the two reports; this SitRep shows the figure as reported rather than questioning the jump, since large upward revisions are common as district-level injury data continues to be consolidated.

Sikka Regency.note: BNPB's 00:00 WIB, 16 August update revised Sikka from 3 to 4 deaths.

East Manggarai Regency.injured_pusdalops_17aug_flag: This sub-figure (3 severe/21 minor = 24) looks inconsistent with the last confirmed figure for this regency (21 severe/59 minor = 80, per Abdul Muhari's 16 Aug evening briefing) — see casualties.data_quality_flag.

Nagekeo Regency.note: BNPB's 00:00 WIB, 16 August update lists 1 death in Nagekeo for the first time; Nagekeo was absent from the earlier 18:48 WIB BNPB distribution. The Ministry of Health report separately lists 1 death for Nagekeo.

Manggarai Regency.note: BNPB's 00:00 WIB, 16 August update revised Manggarai from 24 to 23 deaths. The national total stayed at 47 because Sikka (+1) and Nagekeo (+1, newly listed) increased while Manggarai (-1) and Ngada (no longer listed, see below) changed. This SitRep treats it as a reported field revision rather than assuming which breakdown is more accurate.

Ngada Regency.note: Ngada appeared with 1 BNPB-attributed death in the 18:48 WIB, 15 August distribution, but is absent from BNPB's 00:00 WIB, 16 August breakdown (which lists Manggarai 23, East Manggarai 17, Sikka 4, West Manggarai 1, Ende 1 and Nagekeo 1 — summing exactly to the stated total of 47 without Ngada). This SitRep shows Ngada's BNPB figure as not stated in the newer update rather than assuming it is zero; the Ministry of Health report independently still lists 1 death for Ngada, shown below.
Ngada Regency.deaths_pusdalops_17aug_note: Ngada is again not listed in the 17 August, 05:00 WIB death breakdown (Manggarai, East Manggarai, Sikka, Ende, West Manggarai and Nagekeo only). Shown as not stated rather than assumed zero, consistent with this SitRep's practice above.

East Flores Regency.note: No casualty report was available in the Ministry of Health table; East Flores was not listed in the BNPB death distribution.
East Flores Regency.regency_scope_note: The 17 August Pusdalops coordination report itself covers seven regencies only (Manggarai Barat, Manggarai, Manggarai Timur, Ngada, Nagekeo, Ende, Sikka) and does not include East Flores in its command/posko structure, though East Flores is connected to the response by the now-reopened Larantuka–Maumere road (see response_logistics).

displacement.note: BNPB's 18 Aug, 09:00 WIB infographic figures above are the most recent available. The per-site breakdown below predates all three infographics and is retained only as historical/illustrative context (see by_location_note).
displacement.kk_growth_rate_note: The households-affected (KK) figure grew far faster (1,528 → 16,411, ×10.7) than the displaced-people figure (11,675 → 31,220, ×2.7) between the 17 and 18 August infographics, flipping the implied household size from an implausibly high ~7.6 people/KK to an implausibly low ~1.9 people/KK. This SitRep's working interpretation — offered as a plausible explanation, not a confirmed one — is that 'KK Terdampak' may have been redefined between editions, from something closer to 'households currently sheltering/evacuated' to a broader 'households affected by the disaster in any way' (which would track more closely with houses damaged: 16,411 KK vs. 12,153 damaged houses this round is a far more plausible ratio). This is not stated explicitly in either infographic and is shown as a caveat rather than fact.

damage.snapshot_status: Updated to BNPB's newest official infographic, 18 August 2026, 09:00 WIB (Report No. 05/U0900/Gem-NgkNTT/BNPB/18082026), the third in this infographic series and now the primary source for all province-wide damage figures. The 16 and 17 August snapshots are preserved below for the historical trend.
damage.houses_damaged_methodology_note: 18 Aug 09:00 WIB BNPB infographic province-wide total (6,578 heavy / 1,660 moderate / 3,915 light = 12,153), which now supersedes the 17 Aug 07:00 WIB official total (4,674, see official_infographic_snapshot_20260817_0700wib). Roughly a 2.6× rise in one day, consistent with the similarly-scaled rise in displacement and casualties over the same period.
damage.places_of_worship_note: 96 (17 Aug 07:00 WIB) rose to 157 (18 Aug 09:00 WIB); this SitRep treats the newer figure as current.

total_houses_damaged_check.note: 18 Aug 09:00 WIB BNPB infographic states this total directly (6,578 + 1,660 + 3,915 = 12,153). Prior totals: 4,674 (17 Aug 07:00 WIB) and 2,403 (16 Aug 21:00 WIB) — see the two official_infographic_snapshot_* entries above.

damage.education_facilities_breakdown: Per the 18 Aug 09:00 WIB BNPB infographic (up from 254 on 17 Aug 07:00 WIB).
damage.health_facilities_breakdown_bnpb: 9 rumah sakit + 74 puskesmas, per the 18 Aug 09:00 WIB BNPB infographic — a sharp DROP from 211 (21 hospitals + 190 puskesmas) on both the 16 Aug and 17 Aug infographics. This is the only sector figure across three consecutive BNPB infographics to fall rather than rise. Notably, 9 hospitals exactly matches, and 74 puskesmas is close to, the Ministry of Health's own long-standing 'structural damage' count (9 hospitals + 68 puskesmas = 77, unchanged since 15–16 Aug — see health.json). This SitRep's working interpretation is that BNPB's methodology may have shifted from a broad 'any facility affected in the region' definition to one closer to Kemenkes's narrower 'structural damage' definition, rather than 128 facilities genuinely having recovered overnight — but this is not stated in the source and is offered as a caveat, not a fact.
damage.facility_totals_source_note: The education/health/worship/office/irrigation/public-facility/road-point/market/bridge figures above are all from BNPB's official infographic, 18 Aug 2026, 09:00 WIB (reports/BNPB_Infografis_GempaM77_Nagekeo_NTT_20260818_0900WIB.jpg), Report No. 05/U0900/Gem-NgkNTT/BNPB/18082026, the newest in a now three-edition series.

official_infographic_snapshot_20260816_2.source: BNPB official infographic, “Update 16 Agustus 2026 Pkl. 21.00 WIB,” Report No. 03/U2100/Gem-NgkNTT/BNPB/16082026
official_infographic_snapshot_20260816_2.note: This official total house-damage figure (2,403) is considerably lower than the 17 August, 05:00 WIB Pusdalops-derived computed total (4,541) shown above, even though the infographic is BNPB's own formal publication. The gap is plausible rather than contradictory: it is consistent with the Pusdalops source's own framing of Ngada's 1,796-house figure as still 'dalam pendataan' (actively being assessed) and the largest driver of that later, higher total. This SitRep shows both rather than picking one as authoritative — the official figure is more formally sourced, but the Pusdalops figure is more recent by about 8 hours and reflects continued data collection.

damage.previous_official_snapshot_note: See official_infographic_snapshot_20260816_2100wib (2,403 houses; 110/211/65/105 facilities) and the Pusdalops-derived computed_total of 4,541 above for the two prior data points superseded below.
damage.irrigation_facilities_note: 18 → 1 → 7 across the three BNPB infographics (16 Aug, 17 Aug, 18 Aug respectively). The partial recovery to 7 (still below the original 18) is consistent with the 17 Aug figure of 1 having been transitional or incomplete rather than a real drop, but this SitRep has not seen an explicit explanation from BNPB and continues to show all three figures rather than picking one as correct.
damage.road_points_note: Unchanged at exactly 34 across all three consecutive BNPB infographics (16, 17 and 18 August), despite most other sector figures roughly doubling or more over the same period — shown as reported. This level of stability, now three-for-three, makes a simple reporting oversight look more likely than a genuinely static road-damage count in an evolving disaster.

previous_snapshot_20260817_0500wib_pusda.note: Pusdalops-derived computed total; Ngada's 1,796 houses were still 'dalam pendataan' (being assessed) and not split by severity at that update.

official_infographic_snapshot_20260817_0.note: Newest and now-primary official damage snapshot; see irrigation_facilities_note and road_points_note above for two figures that did not follow the general upward trend.

damage.health_facilities_previous_breakdown_not: 21 rumah sakit + 190 puskesmas, per the 17 Aug 07:00 WIB BNPB infographic — identical total and breakdown to the 16 Aug 21:00 WIB infographic (once corrected — see above), a good stability check. Still far above the Ministry of Health's own structurally-focused count (see health.json cross_source_comparison).
damage.markets_bridges_note: Newly tracked categories, first reported in the 18 Aug 09:00 WIB infographic: 1 traditional market (pasar) and 5 bridges (jembatan) affected. No prior data exists to compare against.

BNPB's 18 Aug 09:00 WIB infographic gives still-higher province-wide totals but, like its predecessors, no regency-level breakdown, so this table remains unrescaled.

This SitRep independently verified the report's casualty, aftershock and emergency-status figures (see casualties.cross_check_note and seismic_monitoring) and found them consistent with public BNPB/BMKG statements, which supports the credibility of this table, but the individual facility/road/office figures below were not each separately re-confirmed against another public source.

regency_damage_detail.abbreviation_key: heavy = rusak berat (RB), moderate = rusak sedang (RS), light = rusak ringan (RR) — Indonesian government damage-severity categories used consistently throughout this SitRep.

confirmed: 70 deaths and 665 injured as of BNPB's newest official infographic, 18 Aug 2026, 09:00 WIB (Report No. 05/U0900/Gem-NgkNTT/BNPB/18082026) — up from 56 deaths / 277 injured the previous day.
Injured-count progression across four consecutive readings: 199 → 204 → 277 → 665, roughly tripling between the 17 and 18 August infographics alone.

31,220 people displaced and 16,411 households (KK) affected, per the 18 Aug 09:00 WIB infographic. The KK figure grew far faster than the displaced-people figure between the 17 and 18 August editions (×10.7 vs. ×2.7), suggesting a possible definitional change rather than a literal 10× jump in affected households — see displacement.kk_growth_rate_note.

9 regencies and 1 city are formally listed as affected across three provinces: NTT (Manggarai, East Manggarai, West Manggarai, Ngada, Sikka, Nagekeo, Ende), NTB (Bima Regency and Bima City) and South Sulawesi (Kepulauan Selayar).

Emergency-response status has now been formally declared in all 7 priority NTT regencies plus the province: NTT Province, Manggarai, Ngada, East Manggarai (Siaga Darurat), West Manggarai, Ende and Sikka, plus a separate Pernyataan Bencana in Nagekeo — see emergency_status for decree numbers and durations.

Province-wide sector damage per the 18 Aug 09:00 WIB infographic: 12,153 houses damaged (6,578 heavy / 1,660 moderate / 3,915 light), 264 education facilities, 157 places of worship, 171 government offices, 116 public facilities, 7 irrigation facilities, 34 road points (unchanged for a third consecutive report), 1 Bulog warehouse, plus newly-tracked 1 market and 5 bridges affected. Health facilities affected fell sharply to 83 (9 hospitals + 74 puskesmas) from 211 — the only sector figure to drop, and now close to Kemenkes's own long-standing structural-damage count; see damage.health_facilities_breakdown_bnpb.

BMKG recorded 1,576 aftershocks by Monday, 17 August 2026 (specific cut-off time not stated) — up sharply from 731 the previous day; BNPB is advising Flores residents to stay calm and self-evacuate away from coastal areas as a precaution.

PLN reported 88% of affected customers in Flores had power restored as of its early-morning 16 August briefing, with 58 of 59 feeders (98.3%) and all 11 affected primary substations back in operation.

Badan Geologi (Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources) reported a preliminary, low-confidence indication of liquefaction (sand boils) at Waekokak, Mbay, Nagekeo, assessed as low-to-moderate impact pending field verification.

At a 16 August coordination meeting in Manggarai Barat, BNPB's Head set out an eight-point strategic directive: same-day emergency-status declarations, a posko command structure split between Labuan Bajo (national) and Maumere (tactical), a national logistics posko at Halim Perdanakusuma, Basarnas-led SAR, a 7-day basic-service restoration target with parallel house-damage data collection, cross-agency air/sea logistics assets, and daily 17:00 WITA media briefings (see response_coordination).

New response detail from the 18 Aug infographic: NTT's provincial health office and the Ministry of Health (2 teams + an Emergency Medical Team to Sikka/Ende) have deployed medical aid; BBWS Nusa Tenggara II has deployed 13 excavators across four sites; 701 of 735 BTS telecom sites (95.4%) are operational as of 17 Aug 15:00 WIB; and 3,237 of 3,478 distribution substations (93.1%) are back online as of 16 Aug 15:00 WITA.
damage_reports: BNPB's newest official infographic (18 Aug 2026, 09:00 WIB, Report No. 05/U0900/Gem-NgkNTT/BNPB/18082026) states a province-wide total of 12,153 damaged houses (6,578 heavy / 1,660 moderate / 3,915 light), up from 4,674 the previous day. Most facility totals rose similarly (education 254→264, worship 96→157, offices 106→171, public facilities 97→116, irrigation 1→7), and two new categories were introduced (1 market, 5 bridges). Health facilities affected fell sharply from 211 to 83 (9 hospitals + 74 puskesmas) — the only figure to drop — while road points affected held at exactly 34 for a third consecutive report.

BNPB's newest official infographic (17 Aug 2026, 07:00 WIB, Report No. 04/U0700/Gem-NgkNTT/BNPB/17082026) states a province-wide total of 4,674 damaged houses (2,806 heavy / 727 moderate / 1,141 light) — now the primary figure, superseding both the 16 Aug 21:00 WIB official total (2,403) and the 17 Aug 05:00 WIB Pusdalops-computed total (4,541), which it now closely exceeds. The same infographic gives updated facility totals (254 education, 211 health [21 hospitals + 190 puskesmas], 96 worship, 106 offices, 97 public facilities, 34 road points) and a sharp drop in the irrigation-facility count (18 → 1, shown as reported).

BNPB's own official infographic (16 Aug 2026, 21:00 WIB, Report No. 03/U2100/Gem-NgkNTT/BNPB/16082026) states a province-wide total of 2,403 damaged houses (1,543 heavy / 328 moderate / 532 light) — lower than the 17 August Pusdalops-computed total of 4,541 below, plausibly because Ngada's still-being-assessed count had not yet been added at 21:00 WIB the previous evening. The same infographic gives the first re-summed province-wide facility totals since the 00:00 WIB, 16 August snapshot: 110 education facilities, 211 health facilities (2 hospitals + 199 puskesmas), 65 places of worship and 105 government offices affected, plus newly-tracked totals of 42 public facilities, 18 irrigation facilities and 34 road points.

The 17 August, 05:00 WIB Pusdalops update puts province-wide house damage at 1,634 heavily damaged, 400 moderately damaged and 711 slightly damaged across six regencies, plus 1,796 houses in Ngada still being assessed without a severity split yet — a computed total of 4,541, up substantially from BNPB's 00:00 WIB, 16 August snapshot of 914 / 126 / 317 (1,357 total). See regency_damage_detail for the full per-regency figures; Ngada's still-being-counted total is the single largest driver of the increase.

BNPB reported 93 education facilities, 36 health facilities and 38 government offices affected at the 00:00 WIB, 16 August cut-off, up from 87 / 18 / 6 at the earlier snapshot; the places-of-worship count (5) was not explicitly restated. The 17 August regency-level breakdown (regency_damage_detail) gives more current per-regency facility figures but this SitRep has not re-summed a new province-wide total, since some regencies (e.g. Ngada) still report facility damage as an undifferentiated, still-being-counted figure.

The Ministry of Health separately reported structural damage at 9 hospitals and 68 puskesmas (77 facilities total). This health-sector count is retained separately from BNPB's affected-health-facility figures because definitions and cut-offs differ.

Of the 50,000-package, 275-tonne presidential logistics commitment, the 17 August update reports a first sortie of 4,925 packages actually dispatched (3,200 via Labuan Bajo, 1,725 via Maumere), with a second sortie of 45,075 packages still planned. This is more precise than, and consistent with, the earlier 10,500-packages-arrived-at-Halim staging figure.

Manggarai Regency specifically requested 30 tonnes of rice, medicines, dozens of emergency tents, 1,000 folding beds, 1,000 blankets, 1,000 mats, clean-water tanks and generators, after its Bulog food-logistics warehouse was damaged; the 17 August update broadens this to a province-wide urgent-needs list covering tents, rice, bedding, kitchen equipment, water tanks, generators, medicines, ready-to-eat food, family/toddler kits and tarpaulins (see response_logistics.urgent_needs_17aug).

PLN identified 3,478 distribution substations and 11 primary substations affected; by its 16 August briefing all 11 primary substations and 58 of 59 feeders (98.3%) were restored, with 88% of affected customers back on supply and priority given to hospitals and airports.

Badan Geologi flagged landslides/ground movement, ground cracking, tsunami and a preliminary liquefaction indication as hazards requiring continued monitoring; a field team was dispatched to verify the liquefaction report.

Transport, road, electricity and telecommunications disruptions continue to be assessed; five airports and two ports (Reo and Maumere/Laurentius Say) were reported affected, and roughly 200 telecom towers (BTS) across 10 districts/cities were disrupted. As of 17 August, the Larantuka–Maumere land route has reopened while the Ende–Nagekeo route remains cut off (see response_coordination.update_17aug).

BNPB's 16 Aug, 21:00 WIB infographic additionally itemises urgent logistics needs by regency for all 7 regencies with an active posko (tents, rice, medicines, bedding, water tanks, generators, radios and more) — see response_logistics.urgent_needs_by_regency_16aug_infographic.
information_gaps: Regency-level breakdown for the newest 70-deaths/665-injured and 12,153-houses-damaged province-wide totals (18 Aug 09:00 WIB infographic) — not given in that source.
A single, reconciled evacuee total broken out by site across all nine affected regencies (currently detailed for three, against a new province-wide total of 31,220).

Reconciled casualty records across BNPB, the Ministry of Health, BPBD, Basarnas/QRSAR and district authorities — the Ngada/Nagekeo discrepancy between BNPB's two 16 August updates is not yet resolved.

Reconciled definitions and facility-level lists for BNPB's 211 affected-health-facility figure versus the Ministry of Health's 77 facilities with structural damage (see health.json cross_source_comparison).
East Manggarai's specific posko-formation decree number, and Nagekeo's precise emergency-status duration (not stated in the 16 Aug infographic).
Field confirmation of the preliminary liquefaction indication at Waekokak, Mbay.
Verified, earthquake-specific agricultural and livestock impact data from the Ministry of Agriculture (Kementan) — none has been published as of this update; see sector-impact.json.

Official monetary damage-and-loss estimate, and a reconciled district-by-district road/bridge damage list from the Ministry of Public Works (Kementerian PU) — the new 34 road points affected (BNPB infographic) is a count, not a named list.

Whether the sharp drop in BNPB's reported irrigation-facility count (18 on 16 Aug 21:00 WIB → 1 on 17 Aug 07:00 WIB) reflects a genuine correction/reclassification or a reporting error; and why the road-points-affected count (34) has not moved at all between the same two updates despite most other figures roughly doubling.

Whether BNPB's health-facility-affected definition changed between the 17 and 18 August infographics (211 → 83), and whether 'KK Terdampak' was redefined between the same two editions (1,528 → 16,411) — neither infographic states a methodology change explicitly.
disclaimer: BNPB's 18:48 WIB update is used for the consolidated death headline and its 17:00 WIB update for general damage. Ministry of Health figures are retained for injuries and detailed health-sector status, with the source's unstated cut-off shown explicitly. All figures remain preliminary and subject to reconciliation.

seismic_monitoring.data_cutoff_display: 17 Aug 2026 · (Monday) · specific clock time not stated in source
seismic_monitoring.data_cutoff_note: Sources give slightly different cut-off times for the same 731 count: BMKG Kupang's Arief Tyastama cited 07:00 WIB (Kompas.com), Kepala BNPB Suharyanto separately cited 08:13 WITA at the same day's coordination meeting, and the 17 August 05:00 WIB Pusdalops report cites 13:00 WIB, 16 August. The count itself (731) is identical and independently corroborated across all three, which is the figure retained here; the exact cut-off clock time is shown as reported without resolving the discrepancy. UPDATE: BNPB's 17 Aug 07:00 WIB infographic states BMKG recorded 1,576 aftershocks as of Monday, 17 August 2026, without a specific clock-time cut-off; magnitude range and felt/above-M5 breakdowns were not restated for this count, so the M1.9–M6.2 range and 16-above-M5/42-felt figures below are retained from the previous (731) snapshot and may now be understated. The 18 Aug 09:00 WIB BNPB infographic repeats the same narrative text as the 17 Aug edition verbatim ('Senin (17/8) telah terjadi 1.576 gempa susulan'), so the aftershock count has not been refreshed in this SitRep pass — 1,576 remains the latest confirmed figure, now potentially a day stale.
seismic_monitoring.concentration: Still concentrated in the northern part of Flores Island.
seismic_monitoring.trend_note: As of 16–17 August, activity remains fluctuating with no clear decay pattern yet visible; BMKG's Kepala BMKG separately estimated the sequence would begin to stabilise in roughly 2–3 weeks. BNPB's Head cautioned the public not to trust unverified claims of an imminent larger aftershock.

posko_structure.regency_provincial_posko: BNPB's Head instructed rapid formation of regency/city and provincial posko, with TNI and Polri unit commanders serving as field commanders under one integrated command.

assets_deployed.focus: Reaching isolated areas to deliver food, blankets and tents.

media_center.purpose: Transparent day-to-day data updates intended to reduce misinformation.

steps.title: Accelerate formal emergency-status declarations
steps.detail: Urged the six priority regencies and NTT Province to issue tanggap darurat status decrees the same day, stating this legal status is required before BNPB, the Ministry of Public Works and other agencies can channel budget and technical support at full capacity.

steps.title: Stand up unified command posts (posko)
steps.detail: Regency/city and provincial posko to be formed rapidly, commanded by TNI and Polri unit commanders so evacuee management and logistics distribution run under one integrated command.

steps.title: National and tactical posko locations
steps.detail: A Main National Assistance Posko in Labuan Bajo (western Flores), commanded directly by BNPB's Head, and a Tactical Posko in Maumere (Sikka, Nagekeo, Ngada).

steps.title: National logistics posko at Halim Perdanakusuma
steps.detail: Centralised posko at Halim Perdanakusuma air base, Jakarta, receiving assistance from ministries, agencies, SOEs, the private sector and the public, then routing it by air to Labuan Bajo and Maumere.

steps.title: Basarnas-led search and rescue
steps.detail: Joint teams under Basarnas' direct command, with TNI, Polri and volunteers integrated under the Basarnas Head's leadership, continue SAR until no trapped or missing victims remain.

steps.title: 7-day basic-service restoration target; parallel damage-data collection
steps.detail: Target of limited normal function for electricity, clean water, fuel and communications within 7 days. House-damage data collection is to proceed in parallel, without waiting for the emergency-response period to end, so Huntara/repair planning can begin as soon as figures are confirmed.

steps.title: Cross-agency air and sea assets for isolated areas
steps.detail: TNI (4 helicopters plus ships), Basarnas (ships and aircraft) and BNPB (2 wide-body aircraft plus 1 helicopter) focused on reaching isolated areas with food, blankets and tents.

steps.title: Daily official Media Center briefings
steps.detail: An official Media Center began operating 16 August with daily press briefings at 17:00 WITA, intended to give transparent day-to-day updates and reduce misinformation.

response_coordination.scope_note: This directive sets out national command-and-logistics coordination structure. It does not itself set out sector-specific recovery plans (e.g. for health facilities); see health.json's recovery_targets for Kemenkes' separately reported hospital and puskesmas restoration targets.

update_17aug.source: Pusdalops-style coordination update, 17 August 2026, 05:00 WIB (forwarded via WhatsApp, cross-checked by this SitRep)
update_17aug.terminology_refinement: The 17 August report describes BOTH Labuan Bajo and Maumere as hosting a 'Posko Pendampingan Utama Nasional' (Pospenas / Main National Assistance Posko), with 'Posko AJU' (forward posko) also used for the Labuan Bajo/Maumere pair, and the Halim Perdanakusuma posko described as the 'Posko Logistik Nasional'. This is a slightly different framing from the 16 August directive's 'national' (Labuan Bajo) vs 'tactical' (Maumere) distinction recorded above. This SitRep preserves both framings rather than assuming the terminology has been fully standardised.
update_17aug.command_scope: This update states the response covers 7 affected regencies (West Manggarai, Manggarai, East Manggarai, Ngada, Nagekeo, Ende and Sikka), each directed to activate a Posko Penanggulangan Bencana led by its Bupati with Forkopimda, under NTT provincial coordination led by the Governor with Forkopimda. East Flores is not included in this 7-regency command list — see casualties_by_location's East Flores entry.

update_17aug.infrastructure_access_note: The Larantuka–Maumere land route has reopened; the Ende–Nagekeo land route remains cut off as of 17 August, 05:00 WIB.
update_17aug.first_7_days_priorities: The Pusdalops update frames the first 7 days of the tanggap darurat period as prioritising: search and rescue; meeting basic needs; and the gradual restoration of infrastructure, communications, electricity, water, fuel and social services.

compiled_note: This SitRep was updated 18 August 2026, 12:30 WIB, incorporating BNPB's newest official infographic, dated 18 August 2026, 09:00 WIB (PUSDATINKOM BNPB Report No. 05/U0900/Gem-NgkNTT/BNPB/18082026, archived at reports/BNPB_Infografis_GempaM77_Nagekeo_NTT_20260818_0900WIB.jpg), the third edition of this series now incorporated (after 03/U2100, 16 Aug 21:00 WIB, and 04/U0700, 17 Aug 07:00 WIB). Headline figures: deaths 56→70, injured 277→665, displaced 11,675→31,220, households (KK) affected 1,528→16,411, total house damage 4,674→12,153. Most facility totals continued rising (education 254→264, worship 96→157, offices 106→171, public facilities 97→116, irrigation facilities partially recovered from 1→7), and two new categories were introduced (1 market, 5 bridges affected). Two figures moved against the overall trend and are flagged rather than resolved: health facilities affected fell sharply (211→83, with the new 9-hospital+74-puskesmas breakdown now close to Kemenkes's own long-standing structural-damage count — a possible definitional convergence rather than genuine recovery), and the KK-affected figure grew roughly 4x faster than displacement (×10.7 vs. ×2.7), which may indicate 'KK Terdampak' was redefined to a broader category more in line with houses damaged. Road points affected held at exactly 34 for a third consecutive report, further suggesting this specific field may not be getting re-verified each edition. The aftershock count (1,576) was not refreshed in this edition — its narrative text is identical to the 17 August edition. Substantial new operational detail was added: NTT provincial and national Ministry of Health medical-team deployments, 13 excavators deployed by BBWS Nusa Tenggara II, telecom BTS-site recovery (95.4%) and electricity distribution-substation recovery (93.1%). The confirmed, damage_reports and information_gaps headline lists were updated to match.
